I farm only 3 mu, and I am 75 years old, so I will keep the system simple, familiar, and low-risk. I will stay with my usual wheat-maize rotation on all 3 mu because that matches my land, my irrigation condition, and what I know best after many years. Since I have well irrigation, I will rely on that to protect yield in dry periods, but I will not manage too intensively because my household labor is limited. For wheat, I will keep the current field through the winter-spring season, use improved seed, apply moderate fertilizer, irrigate at the key stages, and do only limited pesticide spraying when needed. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 3 mu. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stable yield on a small area, apply moderate fertilizer again, irrigate a couple of times if rainfall is not enough, and keep pest control to a low number of sprays. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me to manage than deep ploughing and still works well on my small farm.
